summary: Marek Zemánek works in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed a master's program at Dongguk University, studied at Seoul National University, and completed his dissertation at Charles University under doctoral supervisor Radek Chlup.

Margaret Dornish works in religious studies and sinology. She studied at Yale University, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).
Margaret Gouin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bristol under the doctoral supervision of Paul Williams.

Margaret Mead (1901–1978) studied at Solebury School, DePauw University (~1919–1920), Barnard College (~1920–1923), and Columbia University (~1923–1929). She held posts at the American Museum of Natural History (~1926–1978), Columbia University (~1954–1978), and the University of Rhode Island (~1970–1972).

Margaret R. Miles (born 1937) is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at San Francisco State University and the Graduate Theological Union (~1973–1977), later holding posts at Harvard Divinity School (~1978–1996) and Harvard University (attested 1999).

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower (attested 2016) and conducted postdoctoral study under Xiuping Hong.

Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya (1933–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at St. Petersburg University (~1950–1955), she held long-term posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts and the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1956–2017).
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Karin Preisendanz and completed her MA under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2010).

Maria Heim works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned a BA from Reed College and a PhD from Harvard under Charles Hallisey, also studying under Muni Jambūvijaya, Nagin J. Shah, and W. S. Karunatillake. She taught at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

Marianne Winder (1918–2001) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of London and SOAS, and held posts at the University of Nottingham and the Wellcome Trust (~1964–1983) as Keeper of the Oriental Manuscripts.
Marie G. Wanek is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Pennsylvania and was taught by Sengaku Maeda.

Marina Illich is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University in 2006 under Robert A. F. Thurman, having also studied under Ryuichi Abe, Angela Zito, and John Stratton Hawley.

Mario D'Amato works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, and held posts at Hampshire College (attested 2001) and Rollins College as an assistant professor.
Mario Kozah works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Cambridge under James Montgomery and held a post at the American University of Beirut.

Mario Poceski works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from UCLA in 2000 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and held posts including Visiting Assistant Professor at the University of Iowa (2001) and Assistant Professor at the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).
Marion L. Matics is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under doctoral supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, as well as under teacher Robert A. Fowkes.

Mark A. Nathan specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and held posts at UCLA, Kangwon National University, and the University at Buffalo (all attested 2010).

Mark Allon specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned degrees from the Australian National University and the University of Cambridge under Kenneth Roy Norman (~1989–1994), later working at SOAS (~1994–1997) and the University of Sydney (~2002).

Mark C. Elliott is a scholar in sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He has served as a professor of history at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and as Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University.

Mark Csikszentmihalyi (born 1964) specializes in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He served as an associate professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2003–2006) and became Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at UC Berkeley around 2005.
